- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.

- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

CI or test infrastructure.

## Summary

Add 60 deterministic convolution cases covering forward, data-gradient, and weight-gradient operations, including ReLU and residual-add fusions. Preserve the existing 16 fixed cases and the convolution fuzzer's default behavior.

- Cover FP16 and FP32 forward/data-gradient/weight-gradient cases, plus BF16 weight-gradient residual cases, with FP32 computation across nine configurations.
- Represent fused convolution edge dtypes explicitly, and validate WGRAD residual precision with eight small FP16/BF16 controls using both low-precision and FP32 edges.
- Exercise both virtual and materialized weight-gradient intermediates, checking every exposed output independently.
- Use exact comparisons for the 16 BF16 residual cases: their integer inputs accumulate exactly in FP32, and the reference includes final BF16 rounding.
- Add 40 reference/argument checks covering rounding, residual addition, bias ordering, activation, default behavior, and invalid fusion requests. A separate GPU regression checks the default materialized-edge dtype.
- Keep case seeds independent of table positions and include the shape in every residual case ID.
- Mark the 60-case expansion L1; keep the small precision and helper regressions L0. CI configuration is unchanged.

- `test/python/conv/graph/test_conv_fixed.py` defines the fixed parameter matrix, executes the cases, and checks final and materialized intermediate outputs.
- `test/python/conv/graph/test_conv_fuzzer.py` provides the shared graph and reference helpers. Optional intermediate settings preserve existing defaults; gradient-output ReLU means a pointwise ReLU after convolution/residual addition, not a ReLU derivative.

## Why

Add reproducible coverage for convolution fusions that should run consistently rather than depend on random selection. Reuse the existing graph and reference helpers, check materialized outputs independently, and use cancellation controls that fail when intermediate precision is changed. ReLU alone and integer-only inputs do not establish rounding sensitivity.

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

No public API, binding, or production-library changes. The original 16 fixed cases and generated fuzzer defaults are preserved. Shared helpers reject backward bias epilogues, missing required bias, and intermediate requests for plain convolution before graph setup. Omitting the intermediate dtype keeps FP32 fused edges.

FP32 cases rely on planning-time support checks rather than an unnecessary Ampere minimum. Existing dtype-specific capability gates remain. The eight rounding-sensitive GPU controls qualify WGRAD residual paths, not a universal consumer-precision rule for every convolution engine.

Capability and planning-time support rejections remain skips. Execution failures, non-finite outputs, and numerical mismatches remain failures. This does not expand the library's supported GPU or software configurations.

## Testing

Validated with cuDNN 9.x, serially with test-process isolation disabled:

| GPU | Complete fixed suite | Fixed-suite runtime | Focused fuzzer regression |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| L40S | 125 passed, 0 skipped | 45.25s | 8 passed, 0 skipped |
| H100 | 125 passed, 0 skipped | 14.60s | 8 passed, 0 skipped |
| B100 | 125 passed, 0 skipped | 9.60s | 8 passed, 0 skipped |

The fixed suite includes 85 GPU tests and 40 reference/argument checks: 53 L0 and 72 L1 in total. The focused fuzzer run selects eight existing cases, with 2089 deselected. Each execution run emitted one PyTorch cuBLAS primary-context initialization warning.

Regression checks were observed failing before the fixes. On B100, removing low-precision reference rounding fails all four low-edge controls; introducing premature rounding fails all four FP32-edge controls and six BF16 matrix cases. The unmodified suite passes. Exact BF16 matrix comparisons pass on all three GPUs.

Focused collection confirmed 53 L0 tests, 72 L1 tests, and 125 combined. Focused pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. The 60-case expansion alone remains selectable with `-k test_conv_fixed_expansion_L1`.

Ordinary CI selects L0, not the 60 added L1 cases. Recurring execution of that matrix has not been confirmed and should be arranged before retiring equivalent coverage elsewhere.

From `test/python`:

```bash
CUDNN_TEST_NO_ISOLATION=1 python -m pytest conv/graph/test_conv_fixed.py \
  -o "addopts=" -m "L0 or L1" --tb=short --no-header \
  -p no:cacheprovider --junit-xml=result-junit.xml
```

Focused fuzzer regression, also from `test/python`:

```bash
CUDNN_TEST_NO_ISOLATION=1 python -m pytest -n 0 conv/graph/test_conv_fuzzer.py \
  -o "addopts=" -m L0 \
  -k 'test_conv_random_L0 and (t1_ or t2_ or t3_ or t4_ or t5_ or t6_ or t7_ or t8_)' \
  --tb=short --no-header -p no:cacheprovider --junit-xml=fuzzer-junit.xml
```

This is focused validation, not a full-fuzzer run or a kernel-performance benchmark. Times are pytest-reported suite durations, including setup and reference checks.

Focused formatting and license checks passed. From the repository root:

```bash
pre-commit run --files test/python/conv/graph/test_conv_fixed.py \
  test/python/conv/graph/test_conv_fuzzer.py
git diff --check
```

+                config,
+                X,
+                W,
+                Y,
+                None,
+                cudnn_handle,
+                prior_output,
+                raise_on_unsupported=True,
+                intermediate_dtype=edge_dtype,
+                intermediate_output=intermediate,

## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

CI or test infrastructure.

## Summary

Add 60 deterministic convolution cases covering forward, data-gradient, and weight-gradient operations, including ReLU and residual-add fusions. Preserve the existing 16 fixed cases and the convolution fuzzer's default behavior.

- Cover FP16 and FP32 forward/data-gradient/weight-gradient cases, plus BF16 weight-gradient residual cases, with FP32 computation across nine configurations.
- Represent fused convolution edge dtypes explicitly, and validate WGRAD residual precision with eight small FP16/BF16 controls using both low-precision and FP32 edges.
- Exercise both virtual and materialized weight-gradient intermediates, checking every exposed output independently.
- Use exact comparisons for the 16 BF16 residual cases: their integer inputs accumulate exactly in FP32, and the reference includes final BF16 rounding.
- Add 40 reference/argument checks covering rounding, residual addition, bias ordering, activation, default behavior, and invalid fusion requests. A separate GPU regression checks the default materialized-edge dtype.
- Keep case seeds independent of table positions and include the shape in every residual case ID.
- Mark the 60-case expansion L1; keep the small precision and helper regressions L0. CI configuration is unchanged.

- `test/python/conv/graph/test_conv_fixed.py` defines the fixed parameter matrix, executes the cases, and checks final and materialized intermediate outputs.
- `test/python/conv/graph/test_conv_fuzzer.py` provides the shared graph and reference helpers. Optional intermediate settings preserve existing defaults; gradient-output ReLU means a pointwise ReLU after convolution/residual addition, not a ReLU derivative.

## Why

Add reproducible coverage for convolution fusions that should run consistently rather than depend on random selection. Reuse the existing graph and reference helpers, check materialized outputs independently, and use cancellation controls that fail when intermediate precision is changed. ReLU alone and integer-only inputs do not establish rounding sensitivity.

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

No public API, binding, or production-library changes. The original 16 fixed cases and generated fuzzer defaults are preserved. Shared helpers reject backward bias epilogues, missing required bias, and intermediate requests for plain convolution before graph setup. Omitting the intermediate dtype keeps FP32 fused edges.

FP32 cases rely on planning-time support checks rather than an unnecessary Ampere minimum. Existing dtype-specific capability gates remain. The eight rounding-sensitive GPU controls qualify WGRAD residual paths, not a universal consumer-precision rule for every convolution engine.

Capability and planning-time support rejections remain skips. Execution failures, non-finite outputs, and numerical mismatches remain failures. This does not expand the library's supported GPU or software configurations.

## Testing

Validated with cuDNN 9.x, serially with test-process isolation disabled:

| GPU | Complete fixed suite | Fixed-suite runtime | Focused fuzzer regression |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| L40S | 125 passed, 0 skipped | 45.25s | 8 passed, 0 skipped |
| H100 | 125 passed, 0 skipped | 14.60s | 8 passed, 0 skipped |
| B100 | 125 passed, 0 skipped | 9.60s | 8 passed, 0 skipped |

The fixed suite includes 85 GPU tests and 40 reference/argument checks: 53 L0 and 72 L1 in total. The focused fuzzer run selects eight existing cases, with 2089 deselected. Each execution run emitted one PyTorch cuBLAS primary-context initialization warning.

Regression checks were observed failing before the fixes. On B100, removing low-precision reference rounding fails all four low-edge controls; introducing premature rounding fails all four FP32-edge controls and six BF16 matrix cases. The unmodified suite passes. Exact BF16 matrix comparisons pass on all three GPUs.

Focused collection confirmed 53 L0 tests, 72 L1 tests, and 125 combined. Focused pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. The 60-case expansion alone remains selectable with `-k test_conv_fixed_expansion_L1`.

Ordinary CI selects L0, not the 60 added L1 cases. Recurring execution of that matrix has not been confirmed and should be arranged before retiring equivalent coverage elsewhere.

CUDNN_TEST_NO_ISOLATION=1 python -m pytest conv/graph/test_conv_fixed.py \
  -o "addopts=" -m "L0 or L1" --tb=short --no-header \
  -p no:cacheprovider --junit-xml=result-junit.xml
```

  -o "addopts=" -m L0 \
  -k 'test_conv_random_L0 and (t1_ or t2_ or t3_ or t4_ or t5_ or t6_ or t7_ or t8_)' \
  --tb=short --no-header -p no:cacheprovider --junit-xml=fuzzer-junit.xml
```

This is focused validation, not a full-fuzzer run or a kernel-performance benchmark. Times are pytest-reported suite durations, including setup and reference checks.

  test/python/conv/graph/test_conv_fuzzer.py
git diff --check
```
